problem: Policies trained in simulation transfer poorly to real robots because of visual and actuation gaps, and monolithic end-to-end navigation policies are hard to transfer as a whole.
motivation: Real-world training is costly and risky, so simulation is attractive, but the reality gap remains a major bottleneck. A modular, RGB-only, topological pipeline lets each component be transferred separately with little effort.
key_idea: Build a modular topological image-goal navigation pipeline in iGibson/ROS (image-retrieval localization, passage-detector-weighted Dijkstra planning, GRU behavior-cloned local policy) so each module can be transferred to a real robot separately, using finetuning and adversarial feature adaptation.
insight: Modularity makes sim2real tractable: the passage detector needed only a few hundred real images (acc 0.8981 after finetuning vs 0.6296 for the sim-trained model without finetuning), and the local policy ran unchanged. Map quality strongly affects success (Galatia bad map SR 0.55 vs good map 0.75). Real failures came from actuation mismatch, illumination-sensitive localization, and thin obstacles.
method: Localization: image retrieval with a ResNet18 pretrained on ImageNet and finetuned on room classification (92 rooms across 10 iGibson scenes). Descriptors are max-pooled and L2-normalized from layers 3 and 5, and the nearest topological-map node is retrieved.

Topological map: a directed graph whose nodes are embeddings of 18 images (20° steps) taken at each position. Edges connect nodes within 2.5 m and are weighted by the negative log-likelihood of passage from the passage detector.
Planning: Dijkstra on the graph with passage NLL as edge cost, which finds the most navigable path. It outputs the next local goal node and an absolute angle.
Passage detector: a ResNet18 binary classifier, trained on 4020 synthetic images, that predicts whether the space ahead is navigable. It is used both for edge weights and for local obstacle checks.

Local policy: two GRUs (linear velocity in 3 classes, angular velocity in 5 classes) with a forward-consistency loss following Pathak et al. Trained by behavioral cloning on 2486 ROS-navigation-stack trajectories over 20 scenes, at 10Hz with 50-step sequences. The input is the concatenated 1152-d embedding.
PID and control: a PID orients the robot toward the planned angle, then the policy runs for 12 segments of 5s each.

Sim2real transfer: finetune the passage detector on 252 real images. Adversarial feature adaptation initialized from the sim extractor aligns real features to the sim feature distribution. The local policy is left unchanged and the topological map is built from 20 real positions.

setting.backbone: ResNet18 (ImageNet-pretrained, finetuned) for localization and passage detection; GRU local policy trained from scratch
setting.training_data: iGibson synthetic data: 7092 room-classification images (10 scenes), 4020 passage images, 2486 expert trajectories (20 scenes); 360 real images for real transfer
setting.observation: monocular RGB (480x640) plus a reliable absolute heading angle
setting.action_space: continuous linear x and angular z velocity, discretized into 3 and 5 classes, at 10Hz
setting.privileged: A pre-built topological map of each scene is given, along with a reliable angle estimate; goal images are sampled from the map dataset in real tests.

numbers.extra: pre-built topological map; success within 1.5 m or same node as goal

numbers_note: Real-world navigation was only shown qualitatively (one successful episode, 260 s, no collisions). Real passage-detector results are classification metrics, not navigation metrics.
results: On seven iGibson scenes the pipeline reaches SR 0.52-0.96 (SPL 0.43-0.78), with the best results on Beach (SR 0.96) and the unseen Sasakwa (SR 0.89). Cluttered scenes such as Foyil and Divide drop to about 0.5 SR with many collisions. On the real robot, finetuning the passage detector gave 0.8981 accuracy, and one real episode was completed successfully. No baselines are compared.
limitations: No quantitative real-world navigation evaluation, and no comparison against baselines.
Actuation mismatch, illumination and viewpoint sensitivity of localization, and thin or low obstacles undermined real navigation.
The pipeline needs a pre-built topological map and a reliable heading estimate. Evaluation covers only 7 simulated scenes.
builds_on: Pathak et al. Zero-shot visual imitation (forward consistency)
